# Global Single-Arm Study of Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Pooled Analysis of US and EU Cohorts

## Background

The combination of nivolumab (anti-PD-1) and ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4) has shown promising activity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). NCT03940196 is a global, open-label, single-arm Phase 2 study evaluating nivolumab plus ipilimumab in patients with unresectable HCC who had progressed on or were intolerant to sorafenib. Enrollment occurred simultaneously across sites in the United States and European Union to support global regulatory submissions, with pre-specified geographic stratification for operational purposes.

## Methods

Eligible patients had confirmed unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A liver function, ECOG PS 0-1, and prior sorafenib treatment. All patients received nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks for 4 doses, followed by nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks as maintenance. The regimen was identical across all geographies. US enrollment sites (n=18 centers) and EU enrollment sites (n=14 centers across Germany, France, Italy, and Spain) participated under the same protocol, with geographic cohort as a stratification factor at enrollment. No separate treatment was administered to either geographic cohort; both received the same nivolumab plus ipilimumab regimen per protocol.

## Results

One hundred sixty-eight patients were enrolled: 94 from US sites and 74 from EU sites. All 168 patients received nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg Q3W x4 followed by nivolumab maintenance — the single treatment regimen of this trial. The confirmed ORR in the overall population was 31% (95% CI 24–39). Median overall survival was 22.8 months (95% CI 18.1–27.3). ORR was 32% in the US geographic cohort and 30% in the EU geographic cohort, a difference that was not statistically significant (p=0.81) and consistent with expected regional variability in a single-arm study. Safety was similar across geographic cohorts, with Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events in 37% of US patients and 35% of EU patients.

## Conclusion

Nivolumab plus ipilimumab demonstrated robust and consistent antitumor activity in unresectable HCC regardless of geographic region. The US and EU cohorts represent enrollment strata within a single-arm study receiving the identical treatment regimen, not separate treatment arms. These pooled results support the global activity of this combination in second-line HCC.
